fieldMarks: About 34 cm; ancestral (wild-type) plumage pale gray body with darker head, white rump and two black wing bars
Feral flocks include many other colour forms, some resembling native Band-tailed Pigeon
behavior: Forages mostly by walking on the ground, often in flocks
Eats mostly seeds; away from cities waste grain, grass and other seeds, sometimes berries or acorns; in cities largely food scraps
Not migratory; has good homing ability
habitat: Around cities, farms, cliffs and bridges; most common around cities and in suburbs and farms, occasionally in wild places far from human dwellings. In its native range nested on coastal and inland cliffs and gorges.
range: Native to Eurasia; introduced and established throughout most of the world, including across North America.

lookalikes.name: Band-tailed pigeon
lookalikes.howToTell: Wild native pigeon that some feral Rock Pigeon colour forms can suggest; Audubon gives no further separating marks.
